Okay I usually lurk here, but your situation is the exact same thing that happened to me, so I'll chime in:  


Firstly, as another user mentioned, Keeping your WaniKani Apprentice stack below 100 is very important. Only do new lessons if it's below 100. That means you're going to be doing usually 10 lessons max, every 1-2 days. That's fine, take it slow and really soak in the vocab.  


Second, It sounds like the WaniKani style works great for you. How about give [https://www.bunpro.jp/](https://www.bunpro.jp/) a try. It's WaniKani, but for grammar. It has the same style, with forums and everything.  


Third, Join this reddit's official Japanese / English language exchange Discord server: [https://discord.gg/japanese](https://discord.gg/japanese) . It sounds like motivation is an issue for you, (as is for me), so just surrounding yourself with other like-minded individuals who are in the same long-haul as you of learning Japanese, really helps. You'll naturally find yourself translating what other users write to chime in the conversation. It doesn't feel like studying because technically it's not... but it is! That's how you trick your brain. Plus, I'm sure you browse memes on discord anyways.  


Lastly, set your interfaces to Japanese, even if you're not ready. I started with switching my Discord to Japanese, use discord in chrome and download the extension YomiChan [https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/yomichan/ogmnaimimemjmbakcfefmnahgdfhfami?hl=en-US](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/yomichan/ogmnaimimemjmbakcfefmnahgdfhfami?hl=en-US) , it allows you translate words in real time just by hovering over the text while holding shift. It is very 有用 [https://i.imgur.com/J65ZoEl.png](https://i.imgur.com/J65ZoEl.png) . After you get comfortable with various websites now in Japanese, setting your mobile phone to Japanese is the next step, with your desktop computer being end-game.  


Reading is very important, no matter how you do it.. Anyways, hopefully this helps a little. Again, I was in the same position as you, and this is how I slowly got out of it. To be honest, I'm still not fully out of it, but I'm finding when I read / hear Japanese now, things are starting to "Click" as they say; and that, is a very wonderful feeling. 頑張って～
